ordered_diagnoses: Drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms

s1.syndrome_frame: Severe cutaneous adverse reaction to immunotherapy
salient_findings: Severely pruritic, nontender, erythematous papular and macular eruption
Rash progression despite initial treatment with hydrocortisone and diphenhydramine
Rash reached grade III severity with worsening pruritus
key_facts: 54-year-old man with glioblastoma
Treated with M7824, a bifunctional fusion protein targeting PD-L1 and TGF-β
Rash appeared four weeks after initiation of M7824
No other new medications were being taken
Initial treatment with hydrocortisone 1% cream and oral diphenhydramine
Rash progressed to grade II severity
Doxycycline was started for suspected acneiform eruption
Laboratory evaluation showed no elevations in liver enzymes, no eosinophilia, and no lymphadenopathy
Treated with triamcinolone 0.1% ointment and hydroxyzine
M7824 infusions were held, and prednisone at 40 mg per day was initiated

shortlist.label: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Severe cutaneous adverse reaction with progression to grade III severity

shortlist.label: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
shortlist.why_kept: Severe skin eruption with potential for widespread skin detachment

shortlist.label: Drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms
shortlist.why_kept: Reaction to M7824 with severe pruritus and skin eruption

shortlist.label: Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden onset of widespread pustular eruption after initiation of M7824

shortlist.label: Lichenoid drug eruption
shortlist.why_kept: Pruritic, erythematous papular and macular eruption consistent with drug reaction

raw.rationale: The patient's rash and pruritus progressed despite initial treatment, and laboratory evaluation showed no elevations in liver enzymes, no eosinophilia, and no lymphadenopathy, which is more consistent with a lichenoid drug eruption than other options.

rejected.label: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms did not include mucosal involvement or target lesions, which are characteristic of Stevens-Johnson syndrome.

rejected.label: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms did not include widespread skin necrosis or detachment, which is characteristic of toxic epidermal necrolysis.

rejected.label: Drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms
rejected.why: The patient's laboratory evaluation showed no eosinophilia, which is a key feature of this condition.

rejected.label: Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis
rejected.why: The patient's rash was not pustular, and the condition did not include fever or neutrophilia, which are characteristic of acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis.
